A1.justification: Despite the changed title and position-paper framing, both PDFs describe the same layer-selection method, transition theorem, and experimental program. Their text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–C support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original model-recovery and customization experiments, layer-selection analyses, and adversarial evaluations in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains extensive original experimental results and reports additional DarkneTZ comparisons and customization-versus-placement results, despite being presented as a position paper.

M1.justification: SCARA becomes SOLID, and recovery difficulty becomes distillation difficulty. Both methods evaluate initial loss after randomizing candidate bottom-layer prefixes and select the smallest prefix satisfying the same tolerance threshold. The deployment reframing does not establish a changed algorithm or model architecture.

E1.justification: The sixteen functionality benchmarks and six customization domains remain. However, v2 removes the separate membership-inference evaluation on Ag News, attribute-inference evaluation on PersonalReddit, and prompt-injection evaluation from v1 Table 5 and Appendix B.11, eliminating a distinct family of privacy and adversarial test scenarios.

E2.justification: v2 adds DarkneTZ, protecting the final decoder layer, to the reported attack comparisons in Tables 1–2 and customization comparisons in Figure 5. This is distinct from v1's two-final-layer preliminary experiment. SAP-DP and fully closed/secured comparisons remain, while the adversarial comparison against gold standards in v1 Table 5 disappears.

E3.justification: v2 Section 5.3 and Figure 4 newly report customization while varying the placement of fixed-size secured sets; v1's customization sweep varied bottom-prefix size. The corresponding appendix still describes the prefix experiment. The listed evaluation-set total also changes from 4,066 in v1 Table 9 to 1,516 in v2 Table 5; neither change establishes that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 removes the Gaussian-perturbation error-amplification study in v1 Figure 5/Appendix B.7 and the three adversarial analyses in Table 5/Appendix B.11. It adds customization-versus-placement evidence in Figure 4. Dataset-scale, tolerance-sensitivity, difficulty-correlation, and OPT-350M limitation analyses remain in the appendices.

E5.justification: Removing v1 Figure 5 also removes its box-and-whisker reporting of hidden-state deviation distributions. The main repeated-run arrangements remain unchanged, including seed 42 for the 70B attack experiments and three seeds for smaller models. Pearson/Spearman procedures are retained; their changed coefficient values are result changes.

E6.justification: v2 Table 1 adds DarkneTZ FT-all distillation ratios of 77.9%, 86.5%, 73.7%, and 88.9% for Llama2-70B, Llama2-7B, Mistral-7B, and Phi-2, respectively, while retaining the corresponding SCARA/SOLID performance scores. Some existing correlations change: Mistral-7B's average Spearman coefficient moves from -0.67 in v1 Table 15 to -0.87 in v2 Table 11. New placement/customization findings appear, and the adversarial and error-amplification results disappear.

T1.justification: Theorem 1 now explicitly asserts existence of the normalized limit and replaces identical/nonidentical rows with rank-one/rank-greater-than-one conclusions. The latter conclusion is stronger than v1's nonidentical-row statement. Appendix A otherwise retains the original proof rather than supplying a corresponding new rank argument.

C1.justification: v1 primarily claims an efficient selective closed-sourcing method balancing customization and recovery resistance. v2 makes broader claims about reconciling privacy, model confidentiality, and customization through on-premises deployment, foregrounds final-layer protection failures, and includes a contribution claim that a single carefully chosen layer suffices. The underlying bottom-layer advantage remains.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive arguments about vendor trust, hardware protection, regulation, hybrid deployment, and open-weight model economics, including a new Alternative Views section. It removes v1's explicit limitation concerning membership inference, attribute inference, and prompt injection, along with the SEM error-amplification interpretation. The small-model limitation remains in Appendices B.9 and C.9.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies Xavier initialization and documents the DarkneTZ layer restriction. It removes the project-code link and the construction details and mixture table for the larger attack datasets, although their results remain in Appendix C.6. Most shared training hyperparameters, hardware, software versions, and customization instructions are retained.

R1.justification: Related work is substantially repositioned from customization and model recovery toward data privacy, hardware extraction, trusted execution environments, and on-premises deployment. New references include DarkneTZ, TEESlice, and DeepSeek-R1, supporting a substantially different account of the work's motivation and relationship to prior approaches.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work, threat description, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Experiments are organized around research questions and numbered observations, Alternative Views and an Impact Statement are added, and several former main-text discussions move into the appendices. Terminology changes throughout from SCARA/recovery/closed-source to SOLID/distillation/secured.

P2.justification: The main text changes from a single-column to a two-column layout, with substantial figure and table redesign. Figure 1 becomes a deployment illustration with results, the trade-off plots are reorganized, and customization charts incorporate DarkneTZ. Table 1 changes from five model columns containing three-method comparisons to four model columns containing four-method comparisons; other diagnostic displays are relocated or removed.

improvement.justification: The DarkneTZ comparisons and clearer threat description are useful additions, but v2 weakens claim–evidence alignment and reproducibility. Its stronger rank-greater-than-one claim lacks a matching proof: Appendix A retains a construction with identical columns. It also removes measured privacy/adversarial limitations while broadening privacy claims, and drops construction details for retained large-dataset experiments. These losses outweigh the added comparison coverage.
